subject: GCP private offer: escrowed commit & expedited drawdown request
messages:
From: Liam O'Reilly <liam@cloudbridge.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cloudbridge.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: escrow option + accelerated drawdown for private offer

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — CloudBridge is keen to move forward with a GCP private offer. A couple of asks from procurement that we need to resolve before legal signs off:

1) We'd like the committed credits to be placed in an escrow-like arrangement, where unused committed funds are held for 12 months of drawdown but can be partially reallocated if we expand to additional teams. Is that something Redwood can support on the marketplace/private-offer side?

2) Given Q3 timelines, can we accelerate the drawdown schedule to frontload 40% of committed credits into the first 90 days (with the remainder phased monthly thereafter)? Our CFO prefers earlier consumption for pilot ROI.

Attaching the PO for reference (CloudBridge_PO_v1.pdf). Can you confirm feasibility and any implications for co-sell credits or invoice timing?

Regards,
Liam O'Reilly
Head of Cloud Partnerships
CloudBridge Analytics

--
Attachment: CloudBridge_PO_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: escrow option + accelerated drawdown for private offer

Liam — thanks for the clear asks and the PO. Looping in Marissa (commercial lead) and Jonas (GCP co-sell/partner lead) so we can align on procurement and marketplace constraints.

High level responses:
- Escrow-like arrangements: we don't run an on-platform escrow product, but for private-offers we can negotiate a committed-credit structure with staged invoicing and a contractual reallocation clause — effectively accomplishes the same outcome.
- Frontloading 40% in first 90 days: feasible from a billing/drawdown perspective but there are a few implications: GCP Marketplace billing timing may create a lag for co-sell crediting, and we may need to confirm quota provisioning for the higher early throughput (Jonas can advise on limits).

I'm attaching a proposed drawdown schedule to illustrate how we would phase the commit if we frontload 40% (redwood-drawdown-schedule-v1.xlsx). Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa/Ben to propose commercial language for the reallocation clause and any credit holdbacks.
2) Jonas to confirm GCP marketplace acceptability and whether an escalation to the marketplace rep is needed for accelerated provisioning.
3) I'll coordinate with your procurement to get the PO matched to a DocuSign that captures the reallocation rights.

Marissa / Jonas / Ben — can you take the action items? Liam, can you confirm the PO value and whether CloudBridge legal needs to redline the term sheet?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

--
Attachment: redwood-drawdown-schedule-v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam@cloudbridge.com>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: escrow option + accelerated drawdown for private offer

Liam — appreciate the PO. Confirming PO value: $450,000 (annual committed credits). If we frontload 40% in Q1 of the agreement, the invoicing cadence will need to reflect an initial invoice at execution covering the frontload tranche plus the standard monthly/quarterly billing for the remainder.

Commercial note for procurement: we typically include a reallocation window (12 months) and a one-time reallocation request subject to mutual approval. For faster processing, we'll propose the following clause in the term sheet:
- "Client may request up to 25% reallocation of unused committed credits within the first 12 months; requests above 25% require Redwood approval and may affect co-sell crediting."

Ben — can you draft the clause as contract language and estimate the impact to co-sell credit recognition?

Liam — if acceptable, we'll attach the proposed term-sheet to the DocuSign and kick off redlines.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Liam O'Reilly <liam@cloudbridge.com>, gcp-marketplace-northamerica@google.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: escrow option + accelerated drawdown for private offer

Quick update from the marketplace side after syncing with the GCP rep:
- GCP supports custom billing schedules on private offers but frontloading 40% up-front requires a marketplace-side approval because it changes expected billing profiles. The rep (copied) asks that we submit the proposed schedule and the signed PO; they will stamp the private offer and confirm invoicing flow.
- Co-sell crediting: early heavy consumption can accelerate co-sell recognition but it depends on when GCP attributes consumption vs invoice date. We should expect co-sell credits to trail by ~30 days in the accelerated scenario.

Suggested operational flow:
1) Redwood and CloudBridge agree term-sheet + reallocation clause.
2) CloudBridge returns signed PO.
3) Redwood submits the private-offer request to GCP with the drawdown schedule attached.
4) GCP confirms marketplace acceptance and sends final commit invoice cadence.

I'll take point on filing the marketplace request once we have the signed DocuSign.

-Jonas

--
